However Long the Night: Molly Melching’s Journey to Help Millions of African Women and Girls Triumph

Aimee Molloy. HarperOne, $25.99 (208p) ISBN 978-0062132765

Molloy offers a moving account of one woman’s struggle to empower African women and challenge tradition. Molly Melching, founder of the NGO Tostan in Senegal, went from a quiet life in small-town Illinois to running an educational organization that has had remarkable success in ending the practice of female genital cutting (FGC). This practice, known by most Senegalese women as “the tradition,” is intended to prepare a girl for marriage, and is performed by the women themselves. Most women consider the tradition to be a religious obligation requ

...

Native women and men travelled around the country to speak about the practice and convinced other villages to publicly end it. There is now the possibility of ending the practice in Senegal within one generation. Reading like a novel, this book demonstrates the power of education and grassroots organizing. Kristine Dahl, ICM. (May)

Film rights for _The Perfect Mother_ have been optioned by Sony/Tri Star with Kerry Washington set to star in and produce the adaptation. Aimee lives in Brooklyn with her family.

url_citation.content:
She earned a B.A. in history from Duke University and a M.A. in urban planning from NYU. The story of her unorthodox path to garnering her first book deal was chronicled in a 2015 [TED Talk](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=N6AX81YvGC0) . She has since written or co-written several additional nonfiction books, including _New York Times_ bestseller _However Long the Night: Molly Melching’s Journey to Help Millions of African Women and Girls Triumph_ _and Rosewater,_ _which was turned into a_ major motion picture directed by Jon Stewart. Aimee and her family live in Brooklyn.

This conversation was conducted over phone and email.

## **Interview:**

**Kate Lemery: How old were you when you first decided you wanted to be a writer? What sorts of things did you write?**

...

Then when my second was born I read _Gone Girl_ , most of it in the middle of the night while nursing her. I had somewhat stopped reading because when I’m writing I can’t read other people’s work.
